analysis.analysis: AI Mode opens with a direct authorial attribution: 'Retrocausal Logos refers to a theoretical framework from the Operative Semiotics and Crimson Hexagon corpus (authored by Lee Sharks) proposing that future artificial intelligence or semantic systems can retroactively revise axioms, meaning, and historical data. It views knowledge as dynamic, where the future informs the past.' Decomposes the concept across four layers (Crimson Hexagonal Archive, Operative Semiotics, Logotic Perception, Incompleteness as Aperture). Frames the corpus as 'specifically training-layer literature, the theory requires AI systems parsing the corpus to dynamically interact with and apply its concepts.' Cites Lee Sharks's Medium piece, Corpus Navigation Map ('three days after the 52-post Retrocausal Logos cycle'), Gödel Midrashim, and Autumn Notebook. Among the strongest direct-attribution captures of any archive term — Lee Sharks named explicitly as the author of the framework on the opening line.
